# Model and source

Abrantes 2020 relates the dose of octocog alfa (BAY 81-8973, Kovaltry), a
full-length recombinant factor VIII (FVIII), to plasma FVIII activity and to
the timing and severity of bleeds in patients with severe hemophilia A on
prophylaxis in the three LEOPOLD trials. A two-compartment population PK model
of FVIII activity and a repeated time-to-categorical-event (RTTCE) model of
bleeds were estimated simultaneously: the bleeding hazard is a Gompertz
function of time since study start, inhibited by the individual predicted FVIII
activity, and each bleed is graded mild, moderate or severe by a
proportional-odds model. Covariates were added afterwards with full random
effects modelling (FREM).

The same model, with the same estimates, is the Bayesian prior of the
companion forecasting study (Abrantes 2019), which predicts each patient's
probability of a bleed in the next 24 hours from their PK samples, their bleed
history, or both. Abrantes 2019 prints the PK equations with the IIV and
residual variances (Supplemental Text) and the hazard with its final values
(Equation 1).

Two model files share this vignette:

* `Abrantes_2020_octocogAlfa` -- PK plus the RTTCE model for all bleeds
  (Table 2), the model used in Abrantes 2019.
* `Abrantes_2020_octocogAlfa_jointBleed` -- the same PK with the RTTCE model
  re-estimated on joint spontaneous bleeds in patients aged 12 years or older
  (Table 3).

* Citation: Abrantes JA, Solms A, Garmann D, Nielsen EI, Jonsson S, Karlsson
  MO. Relationship between factor VIII activity, bleeds and individual
  characteristics in severe hemophilia A patients. *Haematologica*.
  2020;105(5):1443-1453.
  [doi:10.3324/haematol.2019.217133](https://doi.org/10.3324/haematol.2019.217133)
* Companion: Abrantes JA, Solms A, Garmann D, Nielsen EI, Jonsson S, Karlsson
  MO. Bayesian forecasting utilizing bleeding information to support dose
  individualization of factor VIII. *CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol*.
  2019;8(12):894-903.
  [doi:10.1002/psp4.12464](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12464)
* Equations: Abrantes 2020 Online Supplementary Appendix, equations 1-12;
  Abrantes 2019 Supplemental Text, equations 1-8, and main-text Equation 1.

```{r load-models}
mod_all <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Abrantes_2020_octocogAlfa"))
mod_joint <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Abrantes_2020_octocogAlfa_jointBleed"))
mod_all_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_all, "omega")
mod_joint_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_joint, "omega")
```

## Model equations

PK, with CL and Q in dL/h, V1 and V2 in dL, the dose in IU and FVIII activity
in IU/dL (Abrantes 2019 Supplemental Text equations 1-8):

$$CL = 1.93 \left(\frac{LBW}{51.1}\right)^{0.646} e^{\eta_{CL}},
\qquad V_1 = 30.3 \left(\frac{LBW}{51.1}\right)^{0.958} e^{\eta_{V1}},
\qquad Q = 1.69,\; V_2 = 6.29$$

$$y = FVIII + (FVIII\,\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2)\, e^{\eta_\varepsilon}$$

Bleeding hazard, per year, with $t$ in years since study start (Abrantes 2020
Supplementary Appendix equations 1-3):

$$h_i(t) = \lambda\, e^{\gamma (t - 1)}
\left(1 - \frac{FVIII_i(t)}{FVIII_i(t) + IF_{50}}\right) e^{\eta_i}$$

$$\lambda = \frac{\lambda_{0.5}\,\lambda_{20}\,(0.5 - 20)}{0.5\,\lambda_{0.5} - 20\,\lambda_{20}},
\qquad IF_{50} = \frac{0.5\,\lambda_{0.5} - 20\,\lambda_{20}}{\lambda_{20} - \lambda_{0.5}}$$

where $\lambda_{0.5}$ and $\lambda_{20}$, the estimated parameters, are the
hazards at a constant FVIII activity of 0.5 and 20 IU/dL one year after study
start.

Bleed severity (equations 6-12), with one random effect shared by both
cumulative logits:

$$\mathrm{logit}\,P(\text{moderate or severe}) = b_1 + \eta_b,
\qquad \mathrm{logit}\,P(\text{severe}) = b_1 + b_2 + \eta_b$$

Probability of a bleed within the next 24 hours (Abrantes 2019 Equation 2):

$$P_i(\text{bleeding}) = 1 - \exp\left(-\int_t^{t+24\,h} h_i(s)\,ds\right)$$

# Population

The analysis pooled LEOPOLD I (NCT01029340, ages 12-64), LEOPOLD II
(NCT01233258, ages 12-64) and LEOPOLD kids (NCT01311648, ages < 12) (Abrantes
2020 Table 1 and Online Table S1): 1535 FVIII activity observations from 183
previously treated patients with severe hemophilia A (endogenous FVIII
< 1 IU/dL) and no inhibitor history, and 633 bleeds from the 172 with a
bleeding observation period. The median patient was 22 years old (range 1-61),
weighed 60 kg (11-124) and had a lean body weight (LBW) of 50.9 kg
(9.25-79.2); 77% were White, 13% Asian, 4.7% Black and 4.7% Hispanic. Doses
were 20-50 IU/kg two to three times a week (LEOPOLD I), 20-40 IU/kg two to three
times a week (LEOPOLD II) and 25-50 IU/kg at least twice a week (LEOPOLD kids).
The median bleeding observation period was 12 months (3.1-13.1); 116 patients
(67%) bled at least once (median 2 bleeds, range 0-33). Of the 633 bleeds, 47%
were mild, 44% moderate and 9.8% severe.

The joint-bleed model re-estimated the RTTCE component on joint spontaneous
bleeds in the 121 patients of LEOPOLD I and II. The forecasting study used the
same 172 patients, split into 51 aged < 12 years and 121 aged >= 12 years.

The same information is available programmatically through each model's
`population` metadata.

# Derived quantities (Tables 2 and 3)

The parameters marked "derived" in Tables 2 and 3 -- $\lambda$ at zero FVIII,
$IF_{50}$ and the typical probabilities of a mild, moderate or severe bleed --
are functions of the estimated parameters. Reading them off the packaged models
checks the reparameterisation (Supplementary Appendix equations 2-3) and the
direction of the severity logits.

```{r derived}
one_row <- data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L, LBM = 51.1)
derived <- function(mod) {
  s <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, one_row, returnType = "data.frame")
  c(
    lam_haz = s$lam_haz, ic50 = s$ic50,
    mild = 100 * s$prob_bleedsev_mild,
    moderate = 100 * s$prob_bleedsev_moderate,
    severe = 100 * s$prob_bleedsev_severe
  )
}
der <- rbind(
  data.frame(model = "All bleeds (Table 2)", t(derived(mod_all_typ))),
  data.frame(model = "Joint spontaneous (Table 3)", t(derived(mod_joint_typ)))
)
der_pub <- data.frame(
  model = der$model,
  lam_haz = c(2.96, 1.80), ic50 = c(10.2, 5.45),
  mild = c(39.6, 30.3), moderate = c(55.7, 65.4), severe = c(4.72, 4.23)
)
der_cmp <- tidyr::pivot_longer(der, -model, values_to = "packaged") |>
  left_join(tidyr::pivot_longer(der_pub, -model, values_to = "published"), by = c("model", "name")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (packaged / published - 1))
der_cmp |>
  mutate(name = dplyr::recode(name,
    lam_haz = "lambda at 0 IU/dL, 1 year (1/year)", ic50 = "IF50 (IU/dL)",
    mild = "P(mild) (%)", moderate = "P(moderate) (%)", severe = "P(severe) (%)"
  )) |>
  dplyr::rename(Model = model, Quantity = name, Packaged = packaged, Published = published, "% difference" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 3, 3, 2))

stopifnot(
  # Deterministic functions of the transcribed estimates; the published
  # values are rounded to three significant figures.
  all(abs(der_cmp$pct_diff) < 1)
)
```

# PK validation

## Terminal half-life at the reported clearances (Figure 3)

Abrantes 2020 reports, from the FREM covariate analysis, a typical CL of
2.30 dL/h at a von Willebrand factor level of 64% (5th percentile) with a
terminal half-life of 11.6 h, and 1.59 dL/h at 179% (95th percentile) with
16.5 h. With V1, Q and V2 at their typical values, the terminal half-life is a
function of the disposition parameters only, so setting CL to these values
checks V1, Q and V2. A single 50 IU/kg dose (3000 IU) is given to a 60-kg
adult at the reference LBW of 51.1 kg and the half-life is estimated with
PKNCA.

```{r halflife}
hl_cases <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Typical (CL 1.93 dL/h)", "vWF 64% (CL 2.30 dL/h)", "vWF 179% (CL 1.59 dL/h)"),
  cl = c(1.93, 2.30, 1.59),
  half.life = c(NA, 11.6, 16.5)
)
obs_hl <- c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 96, 120)
sim_hl <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(hl_cases)), function(i) {
  ev <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = 0, amt = 3000, cmt = "central", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = i, time = obs_hl, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  )
  ev$LBM <- 51.1
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_all_typ, ev, params = c(lcl = log(hl_cases$cl[i])), returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(id = i, treatment = hl_cases$treatment[i])
}))

conc_hl <- sim_hl |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, treatment, time, Cc)
dose_hl <- data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(hl_cases)), treatment = hl_cases$treatment, time = 0, amt = 3000)
nca_hl <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_hl, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_hl, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))

ref_hl <- hl_cases |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(half.life)) |>
  select(treatment, half.life)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_hl, ref_hl,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h")
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PKNCA terminal half-life (packaged model) vs the half-lives reported with Figure 3 of Abrantes 2020.")
```

```{r halflife-check}
hl_res <- as.data.frame(nca_hl$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  left_join(ref_hl, by = "treatment")
hl_res |>
  select(treatment, PPORRES, half.life) |>
  dplyr::rename(Scenario = treatment, "Simulated t1/2 (h)" = PPORRES, "Published t1/2 (h)" = half.life) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value solves; the published values are rounded to
  # 0.1 h, so 3% admits rounding and the terminal-phase regression.
  all(abs(hl_res$PPORRES[!is.na(hl_res$half.life)] / hl_res$half.life[!is.na(hl_res$half.life)] - 1) < 0.03)
)
```

## Virtual cohort and individual clearance

Abrantes 2020 reports a median individual CL of 1.80 dL/h (range 0.579-4.73)
and V1 of 29.5 dL (5.68-51.1) across the estimation cohort. A virtual cohort of
the same age mix is built from the LBW summary of Online Table S1 (normal
within each age group, truncated to the observed range): 24 patients aged 0-<6
years, 27 aged 6-<12, 18 aged 12-<18 and 103 aged >= 18 years, each scaled by
two so the cohort has 344 patients.

```{r cohort}
lbw_groups <- data.frame(
  group = c("0-<6 years", "6-<12 years", "12-<18 years", ">=18 years"),
  n = 2 * c(24, 27, 18, 103),
  mean = c(17.6, 28.4, 52.5, 56.2), sd = c(3.88, 8.55, 9.79, 8.25),
  lo = c(10.1, 9.25, 39.4, 35.5), hi = c(30.1, 48.9, 77.0, 79.2)
)
draw_trunc <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  p <- runif(n, pnorm(lo, mean, sd), pnorm(hi, mean, sd))
  qnorm(p, mean, sd)
}
cohort <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(lbw_groups)), function(i) {
  g <- lbw_groups[i, ]
  data.frame(group = g$group, LBM = draw_trunc(g$n, g$mean, g$sd, g$lo, g$hi))
})) |>
  mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())

ev_coh <- cohort |>
  transmute(id, time = 0, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L, LBM)
sim_coh <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_all, ev_coh, returnType = "data.frame")
ind_par <- sim_coh |>
  summarise(
    median_cl = median(cl), min_cl = min(cl), max_cl = max(cl),
    median_vc = median(vc), min_vc = min(vc), max_vc = max(vc)
  )
data.frame(
  Parameter = c("CL (dL/h)", "V1 (dL)"),
  "Simulated median" = c(ind_par$median_cl, ind_par$median_vc),
  "Simulated range" = c(
    sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", ind_par$min_cl, ind_par$max_cl),
    sprintf("%.1f-%.1f", ind_par$min_vc, ind_par$max_vc)
  ),
  "Published median" = c(1.80, 29.5),
  "Published range" = c("0.579-4.73", "5.68-51.1"),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # The published medians are of empirical Bayes estimates (shrinkage 10-16%)
  # in the real cohort, so only a structural miss -- a wrong exponent,
  # centring weight or typical value -- is screened for.
  abs(ind_par$median_cl / 1.80 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(ind_par$median_vc / 29.5 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

# Bleeding RTTCE validation

## Hazard at a constant FVIII activity (Discussion)

The Discussion gives the typical hazard at the end of the study (one year) as
2.7, 2.0 and 1.2 per year at constant FVIII activities of 1, 5 and 15 IU/dL,
and 5.0 per year at the start and 2.8 per year at the end of the study at
0.5 IU/dL. These follow from the hazard function with the packaged parameters.

```{r hazard-constant}
pars_all <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_all_typ, one_row, returnType = "data.frame")
haz_const <- function(fviii, t_year, p) {
  p$lam_haz * exp(p$gam_haz * (t_year - 1)) * (1 - fviii / (fviii + p$ic50))
}
gam_all <- mod_all$iniDf$est[mod_all$iniDf$name == "gam_haz"]
p_all <- list(lam_haz = pars_all$lam_haz, ic50 = pars_all$ic50, gam_haz = gam_all)
haz_tab <- data.frame(
  scenario = c("1 IU/dL, 1 year", "5 IU/dL, 1 year", "15 IU/dL, 1 year", "0.5 IU/dL, study start", "0.5 IU/dL, 1 year"),
  fviii = c(1, 5, 15, 0.5, 0.5),
  t_year = c(1, 1, 1, 0, 1),
  published = c(2.7, 2.0, 1.2, 5.0, 2.8)
) |>
  mutate(packaged = haz_const(fviii, t_year, p_all))
haz_tab |>
  select(scenario, packaged, published) |>
  dplyr::rename(Scenario = scenario, "Packaged hazard (1/year)" = packaged, "Published (1/year)" = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # Published to two significant figures.
  all(abs(haz_tab$packaged - haz_tab$published) < 0.06)
)
```

## Cumulative bleeds at maintained troughs (Figure 5)

Figure 5 of Abrantes 2020 simulates one year of 420, 1260, 2100 or 6240 IU
every two days in a median 60-kg patient, regimens stated to give
steady-state troughs of 1, 3, 5 and 15 IU/dL. The median cumulative number of
bleeds ranged from 2.73 (trough 1 IU/dL) to 0.745 (trough 15 IU/dL), 1.53 at a
trough of 5 IU/dL, and the 90th percentile from 11.2 to 3.00 (6.17 at
5 IU/dL), "assuming only inter-individual variability on the bleeding hazard
unexplained by any covariates" -- the 111% CV left after FREM, not the 136%
marginal IIV of Table 2.

For a hazard without a Markov term, the expected number of bleeds over a
period is the cumulative hazard, and the random effect multiplies it. The
typical-value cumulative hazard is therefore the median, and the 90th
percentile is the median times $\exp(1.2816\,\omega)$. The typical patient is
given the median LBW of 50.9 kg.

```{r figure5}
fig5 <- data.frame(
  dose = c(420, 1260, 2100, 6240),
  trough_pub = c(1, 3, 5, 15),
  median_pub = c(2.73, NA, 1.53, 0.745),
  p90_pub = c(11.2, NA, 6.17, 3.00)
)
t_trough <- 48 * 180 - 1e-6
sim_fig5 <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fig5)), function(i) {
  ev <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = seq(0, 8760 - 48, by = 48), amt = fig5$dose[i], cmt = "central", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = i, time = sort(c(seq(0, 8760, by = 4), t_trough)), amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  )
  ev$LBM <- 50.9
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_all_typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(id = i, dose = fig5$dose[i])
}))
z90 <- qnorm(0.9)
fig5_res <- sim_fig5 |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(
    trough = Cc[abs(time - t_trough) < 1e-3][1],
    median = cumhaz[time == 8760]
  ) |>
  left_join(fig5, by = "dose") |>
  mutate(
    p90_111 = median * exp(z90 * 1.11),
    p90_136 = median * exp(z90 * 1.36)
  )
fig5_res |>
  select(dose, trough, trough_pub, median, median_pub, p90_111, p90_pub, p90_136) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose every 48 h (IU)" = dose,
    "Trough (IU/dL)" = trough,
    "Published trough" = trough_pub,
    "Median bleeds, 1 year" = median,
    "Published median" = median_pub,
    "90th pct (IIV 111%)" = p90_111,
    "Published 90th pct" = p90_pub,
    "90th pct (IIV 136%)" = p90_136
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # Troughs: deterministic PK, published to the integer.
  all(abs(fig5_res$trough / fig5_res$trough_pub - 1) < 0.03),
  # Medians and 90th percentiles of a 2000-replicate simulation, read from
  # the source's text; the trough-1 median is the furthest off (see
  # Assumptions and deviations).
  all(abs(fig5_res$median / fig5_res$median_pub - 1) < 0.08, na.rm = TRUE),
  all(abs(fig5_res$p90_111 / fig5_res$p90_pub - 1) < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

```{r figure5-plot, fig.height = 4}
sim_fig5 |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(paste0(dose, " IU q48h"), levels = paste0(fig5$dose, " IU q48h"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, cumhaz, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since study start (days)", y = "Median cumulative number of bleeds",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates the median curves of Figure 5 of Abrantes 2020 (typical patient, LBW 50.9 kg)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Stochastic cohort: simulated bleed counts

A stochastic check of the full random-effect model: 200 virtual patients at the
2100 IU every-48-h regimen, with all random effects drawn. Given each
patient's cumulative hazard, the number of bleeds in the year is Poisson. The
expected median count is lower than the typical cumulative hazard because the
136% IIV is wide and the count is discrete.

```{r cohort-bleeds}
n_sub <- 200
ev_vpc <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(n_sub), function(i) {
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = seq(0, 8760 - 48, by = 48), amt = 2100, cmt = "central", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = i, time = c(seq(0, 8736, by = 24 * 7), 8760), amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  )
}))
ev_vpc$LBM <- 50.9
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_all, ev_vpc, returnType = "data.frame")
year_end <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 8760) |>
  mutate(n_bleeds = rpois(dplyr::n(), cumhaz))
summary_vpc <- data.frame(
  statistic = c("Median cumulative hazard", "Median bleed count", "Patients with no bleed (%)"),
  value = c(median(year_end$cumhaz), median(year_end$n_bleeds), 100 * mean(year_end$n_bleeds == 0))
)
summary_vpc |>
  dplyr::rename(Statistic = statistic, Value = value) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  # Centre of a 200-patient cohort; the typical value is 1.53.
  abs(median(year_end$cumhaz) / 1.53 - 1) < 0.45
)
```

```{r cohort-plot, fig.height = 4}
sim_vpc |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(cumhaz, 0.1), p50 = median(cumhaz), p90 = quantile(cumhaz, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since study start (days)", y = "Cumulative hazard (expected bleeds)",
    caption = "Median and 10th-90th percentiles, 200 virtual patients, 2100 IU every 48 h (IIV 136%)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Bleed severity

The typical probabilities of a mild, moderate or severe bleed (39.6, 55.7 and
4.72%) are those at $\eta_b = 0$. Averaging over the severity random effect
(SD 1.67) gives the population proportions, which can be set against the
observed 47% mild, 44% moderate and 9.8% severe bleeds of Table 1.

```{r severity}
marg_sev <- function(b1, b2, sd) {
  f <- function(fn) integrate(function(e) fn(e) * dnorm(e, 0, sd), -Inf, Inf)$value
  p_ms <- f(function(e) plogis(b1 + e))
  p_s <- f(function(e) plogis(b1 + b2 + e))
  100 * c(mild = 1 - p_ms, moderate = p_ms - p_s, severe = p_s)
}
sev_tab <- data.frame(
  category = c("Mild", "Moderate", "Severe"),
  typical = c(39.6, 55.7, 4.72),
  marginal = unname(marg_sev(0.424, -3.43, 1.67)),
  observed = c(46.6, 43.6, 9.8)
)
sev_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Severity = category, "Typical (Table 2, %)" = typical,
    "Averaged over IIV (%)" = marginal, "Observed (Table 1, %)" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  # Every observed proportion within 6 percentage points of the
  # IIV-averaged model; the typical values alone miss severe bleeds by half.
  all(abs(sev_tab$marginal - sev_tab$observed) < 6)
)
```

# Bayesian bleed forecasting (Abrantes 2019)

Abrantes 2019 used this model to forecast, every 24 hours, the probability of a
bleed in the next 24 hours (Equation 2). In the "Bleed" information scenario
only the bleed history updates the hazard random effect $\eta$. Because $\eta$
multiplies the whole hazard, the log posterior of $\eta$ given $k$ bleeds up
to time $t$ is, apart from terms free of $\eta$,
$k\,\eta - H(t)\,e^{\eta} - \eta^2 / (2\omega^2)$, where $H(t)$ is the
typical-value cumulative hazard. Its maximum (the empirical Bayes estimate used
by the source) solves $k - H(t)\,e^{\eta} - \eta / \omega^2 = 0$.

The example below, in the spirit of Figure 2 of Abrantes 2019, follows a
typical-PK adult (LBW 51.1 kg) on 30 IU/kg (1800 IU) every Monday, Wednesday
and Friday for 12 weeks, without bleeds or with bleeds on days 7 and 49, and
forecasts the next-day bleeding probability with the typical $\eta$ (the "PK"
scenario with typical PK) and with the bleed-updated $\eta$ ("Bleed").

```{r forecast}
dose_days <- sort(c(seq(0, 83, by = 7), seq(2, 83, by = 7), seq(4, 83, by = 7)))
ev_fc <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1, time = dose_days * 24, amt = 1800, cmt = "central", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
  data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 84 * 24, by = 24), amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
)
ev_fc$LBM <- 51.1
sim_fc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_all_typ, ev_fc, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::filter(!duplicated(time))
omega2 <- 1.36^2
eta_map <- function(k, H) {
  uniroot(function(e) k - H * exp(e) - e / omega2, c(-20, 20))$root
}
forecast_pat <- function(bleed_days, label) {
  day <- 1:83
  H_t <- sim_fc$cumhaz[match(day * 24, sim_fc$time)]
  H_next <- sim_fc$cumhaz[match((day + 1) * 24, sim_fc$time)] - H_t
  k <- vapply(day, function(d) sum(bleed_days <= d), numeric(1))
  eta <- mapply(eta_map, k, H_t)
  data.frame(
    patient = label, day = day,
    PK = 1 - exp(-H_next),
    Bleed = 1 - exp(-H_next * exp(eta))
  )
}
fc <- bind_rows(
  forecast_pat(numeric(0), "No bleeds"),
  forecast_pat(c(7, 49), "Bleeds on days 7 and 49")
)
fc |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(PK, Bleed), names_to = "scenario", values_to = "p") |>
  ggplot(aes(day, p, colour = scenario)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~patient) +
  labs(
    x = "Study day", y = "P(bleed in the next 24 h)", colour = "Information",
    caption = "In the spirit of Figure 2 of Abrantes 2019 (typical PK, illustrative bleed histories)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

no_bleed <- dplyr::filter(fc, patient == "No bleeds")
with_bleed <- dplyr::filter(fc, patient == "Bleeds on days 7 and 49")
stopifnot(
  # Without bleeds the Bleed forecast falls below the PK forecast as days pass.
  no_bleed$Bleed[no_bleed$day == 80] < no_bleed$PK[no_bleed$day == 80],
  # A bleed raises the Bleed forecast above the bleed-free forecast.
  with_bleed$Bleed[with_bleed$day == 8] > no_bleed$Bleed[no_bleed$day == 8],
  # Daily probabilities of the order of the optimal thresholds of Table 2
  # (0.0058-0.014): bleeds occurred on about 1% of forecast days.
  median(no_bleed$PK) > 0.001, median(no_bleed$PK) < 0.05
)
```

As in the source, the PK-only forecast follows the dosing schedule and does not
react to bleeds, while the bleed-informed forecast falls during bleed-free
periods and rises after each bleed.

# Joint spontaneous bleeds (Table 3)

The joint-bleed model uses the same PK, with lower hazards ($\lambda_{0.5}$
1.65, $\lambda_{20}$ 0.386 per year) and a lower $IF_{50}$ (5.45 IU/dL),
"reflecting less frequent events and higher potency for the replacement
therapy". The typical one-year cumulative hazards for the Figure 5 regimens:

```{r joint}
sim_joint <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(fig5)), function(i) {
  ev <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = i, time = seq(0, 8760 - 48, by = 48), amt = fig5$dose[i], cmt = "central", evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_),
    data.frame(id = i, time = 8760, amt = 0, cmt = NA_character_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  )
  ev$LBM <- 50.9
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_joint_typ, ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(dose = fig5$dose[i])
}))
joint_tab <- sim_joint |>
  select(dose, joint = cumhaz) |>
  left_join(select(fig5_res, dose, all = median), by = "dose")
joint_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose every 48 h (IU)" = dose,
    "Joint spontaneous bleeds, 1 year" = joint,
    "All bleeds, 1 year" = all
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(joint_tab$joint < joint_tab$all))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariates.** The FREM covariate model (von Willebrand factor and race on
  CL; pre-study bleeds on the hazard; age and von Willebrand factor on
  severity) is not encoded: FREM expresses covariate effects through the
  covariance between covariate and parameter random effects, and neither paper
  publishes that matrix, the covariate means or variances. Only correlation
  coefficients (Figure 2) and graphical effect sizes (Figure 3) are given. The
  covariates are documented in `covariatesDataExcluded`, and the IIV in both
  files is the Table 2 / Table 3 marginal IIV (136% on the all-bleeds hazard),
  which is the value Abrantes 2019 quotes in its Equation 1. With all
  covariates, the unexplained IIV on the hazard falls to 111% (Abrantes 2020
  Results); Figure 5 uses that residual value.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports IIV as %CV. The Abrantes 2019 Supplemental
  Text gives the variances behind the PK rows (0.0913, 0.0226 and 0.398), which
  equal (%CV/100)^2. The same convention is applied to the hazard (136% gives
  1.8496) and to the severity SD (1.67 gives 2.7889). The Figure 5 ratio of the
  90th percentile to the median (about 4.1) implies an SD of about 1.1 on the
  log hazard, which matches the 111% residual CV read on this convention.
* **Residual error labels.** The Abrantes 2019 Supplemental Text gives the
  residual variances as 2.31 (proportional) and 0.0411 (additive). These are
  1.52^2 and 0.203^2, so the labels are swapped: Table 2 of Abrantes 2020 gives
  an additive SD of 1.52 IU/dL and a proportional CV of 20.3%, which are used.
* **Rounding.** The LBW exponents are taken from Table 2 (0.646 and 0.958);
  the Abrantes 2019 Supplemental Text prints them rounded to 0.65 and 0.96.
* **Severity parameterisation.** The source models the logits of P(moderate or
  severe) and P(severe). The library's proportional-odds convention models the
  cumulative probability from the lowest grade, so `logite0` = -b1 and
  `logitstep1` = -b2. The random effect changes sign, which leaves the model
  unchanged because its distribution is symmetric. The ordinal output
  `bleedsev` is 1 = mild, 2 = moderate, 3 = severe, and is meaningful only on
  rows where a bleed occurs.
* **Time scale.** The hazard parameters are per year and the Gompertz time is
  years since study start; model time is hours, converted with 8760 h per year
  (365 days). The year length is not stated in the source; 365.25 days would
  change the hazard by less than 0.1%.
* **Administration.** Doses are given as intravenous boluses into `central`;
  the infusion duration is not part of the source model.
* **Study start.** The Gompertz term and the cumulative hazard start at model
  time 0, which must be the patient's study start. To forecast from a later
  time, take differences of `cumhaz` as in Equation 2 of Abrantes 2019.
* **Figure 5 medians.** The trough-1 IU/dL median (2.88 against 2.73 printed)
  is the furthest from the source, about 5%; the troughs themselves and the
  medians at 5 and 15 IU/dL are within 1%. The source medians are summaries of
  2000 simulated patients and the exact regimen start (first dose or steady
  state) is not stated.
* **Below-quantification samples.** How the source handled FVIII activity
  below the quantification limit in estimation does not affect simulation and
  is not encoded.
* **Joint-bleed model population.** The number of bleeds that were both joint
  and spontaneous is not reported; Table 1 gives joint and spontaneous counts
  separately. No covariate model was reported for the joint-bleed
  re-estimation.
* **Bayesian forecasting.** The forecasting study's predictive-performance
  results (ROC and precision-recall areas, Table 2 of Abrantes 2019) depend on
  the individual LEOPOLD data and are not reproduced. The forecasting section
  above illustrates the mechanism only.
